answer: A collateralized deposit mechanism counters Sybil attacks by requiring agents to bond capital along a spiral fee curve before coordinating economic tasks, such as autonomous supply logistics for an orchard or settlement tracking for synthetic onyx. An attacker incurs the verifiable financial opportunity cost of locked liquidity and non-refundable slashing risk per registered identity. However, this creates severe capital inefficiency and unfairly excludes resource-constrained open-source agents.
